lines.text: I need to plan a listening lesson for my CELTA course.
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Okay so for the listening lesson, I was just going to play the recording like five times until they get it. Foolproof, right?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Please don’t. If you play it five times you’re not testing listening, you’re testing memory. One play for gist, that’s it.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Should I at least get them to guess what it’s about first, from a picture or the title?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Yes, that’s prediction, and it primes them before they’ve heard a single word.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Fine. But can I pre-teach every single word first, just so nothing surprises them?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Also no! Only the words they truly can’t survive without. Otherwise you’ve taught a vocab lesson wearing a listening costume.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: A listening costume. Great. And should I record this myself, or find something real?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Authentic audio if you can get it: a real recording beats a scripted one every time.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Okay: lead-in, prediction, pre-teach, then play once for gist. What am I even asking them, “did you enjoy that”?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Close! Something broad: who’s talking, where are they, what’s the general idea. Save the tricky detail questions for later.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Later meaning... a second play? I thought you just told me off for replaying it.
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Different task, different rules. For detail work, a replay or two is totally fair: that’s the harder listening, they’ve earned it.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Okay so once they’ve got their answers, I just tell them if they’re right?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Nope, get them to peer check with each other first. Way less scary than you looming over them with the answer key.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: I don’t loom! ...okay maybe a little. And after all that, we’re done?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Almost: give them a follow-up task tied to the content, so the listening actually leads somewhere instead of just ending.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Should I scaffold any of this, or just throw them in?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: A bit of scaffolding helps: give them the questions before they listen, not after.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: What about jigsaw listening, is that for another day?
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Definitely another day: that’s each pair hearing a different half of the audio, then piecing it together.
lines.speaker: man
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.

lines.text: Oh, two by two, thank you very much, that actually sounds pretty easy now.
lines.speaker: woman
lines.how: One line of a friendly, casual conversation between two colleagues.
